description: AstroPulse is an intelligent health monitoring platform designed for astronauts on long-duration space missions. By combining real-time health data, AI-powered anomaly detection, and interactive analytics, AstroPulse helps identify physiological changes, monitor vital signs, and provide actionable health insights. Our mission is to support astronaut well-being and make space exploration safer through technology and innovation.
summary:
AstroPulse is an interactive mission-control prototype for monitoring crew health during long-duration space missions. Using simulated telemetry from the fictional Aurora-01 mission, it brings crew vitals, sleep trends, cabin conditions, and alerts into one dashboard. Users can compare readings with each astronaut’s personal baseline and ask Starlary, the onboard assistant, why a reading was flagged for review.

The prototype also brings real NASA resources into the experience. It queries NASA DONKI for space weather events and NASA RadLab for historical radiation measurements from the International Space Station. A NASA briefing connects the dashboard concept to wearable technology used in space research. AstroPulse shows how mission teams could spot changes sooner, understand why they matter, and prioritize which readings to review.
details:
AstroPulse demonstrates a crew health review workflow for Aurora-01, a fictional long-duration space mission with three crew members. The mission overview brings key readings into one place. Users can open individual crew profiles, explore vital signs and sleep trends, and see which simulated readings have been flagged for review. Comparing each astronaut’s readings with their personal baseline helps users understand why a change may deserve attention.

Starlary, an interactive assistant represented by an animated star mascot, explains flagged readings and summarizes trends from the simulated dashboard. Status labels, trend charts, and interactive 3D cabin and mission views help users move from a mission-wide overview to a specific reading. The workflow is designed to support human review.

We built the web prototype with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The Cabin & Radiation view queries NASA’s DONKI API for solar flare and geomagnetic storm records and NASA RadLab for historical absorbed radiation dose-rate measurements from DosTel instruments aboard the International Space Station. The NASA Briefing draws on NASA’s article about wearable technology in space station research. The interface labels the fictional crew and cabin telemetry as simulated and identifies the NASA records by source.

We used OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Anthropic’s Claude as development assistants to draft and refine portions of the prototype’s code. We also used ChatGPT’s image generation to create fictional astronaut portraits and visual assets for Starlary, including different expressions and poses.

Our design goal was to help mission teams quickly understand what changed, who is affected, and which readings to review first.
dataRefs: Wearable Tech for Space Station Research
